title: Choosing a thinning method
text: zhang_suen default matches EBImage::thinImage() behavior. thinImage() wrapper provided drop-replacement. lee 2-D adaptation Lee’s original 3-D algorithm. 3-D case (volumetric thinning) implemented release. hilditch method implements parallel form commonly cited “Hilditch” modern image-processing surveys; Hilditch’s 1969 paper actually describes sequential algorithm within-pass deletion tracking different crossing-number definition. See Lam, Lee & Suen (1992) relationship two. K3M lookup tables A_0 … A_5 reproduced Saeed et al. (2010), Section 3.3, page 327. OPTA’s safe-point boolean expression Holt’s condition H taken original papers; Lam-Lee-Suen 1992 survey used cross-reference one transcription error Holt’s middle clause (north vs east) corrected original.

title: Choosing a thinning method
text: thinning algorithms produce broadly similar skeletons V — collapse two diagonal strokes single lines meet bottom. Differences show complex shapes: zhang_suen aggressive simple shapes. guo_hall k3m preserve corners marginally better. hilditch look-ahead crossing-number check, gives different connectivity properties junctions. holt uses edge information neighbouring pixels rather crossing-number check central pixel; specifically designed preserve 2-pixel-wide lines.

title: Choosing a thinning method
text: zhang_suen — default. predictable behavior. Use general purpose thinning compatibility code previously used EBImage::thinImage(). guo_hall — try skeletons lots diagonal features Zhang-Suen breaking corners. lee — want directional processing (four sub-iterations per pass, one per cardinal direction). Sometimes produces cleaner skeletons asymmetric inputs. k3m — strongest corner preservation published comparative studies, cost slower (six phases per outer iteration vs. two Zhang-Suen). hilditch — well-cited historical algorithm; look-ahead crossing-number check makes connectivity slightly different parallel algorithms. opta — one-pass safe-point algorithm. N2 condition protects two-4-adjacent-pixel diagonal patterns, can leave stray pixels bar corners (documented property SPTA). holt — 2-pixel-wide lines preserved. algorithm uses edge information neighbouring pixels 5x5 window, allowing single subcycle.

title: Choosing a thinning method
text: simple bench::mark() comparison moderate image (illustrative): thinning algorithms O(iterations × pixels). Constant factors smallest zhang_suen guo_hall; holt k3m expensive look-aheads. Euclidean distance transform O(pixels) via Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher; medial axis O(pixels) since just adds single linear pass DT. 200×200 images algorithms finish milliseconds modern hardware.
code: library(bench) m <- matrix(0L, 200, 200) m[50:150, 50:150] <- 1L  # solid square  bench::mark(   zs       = thin(m, method = "zhang_suen"),   gh       = thin(m, method = "guo_hall"),   hild     = thin(m, method = "hilditch"),   k3m      = thin(m, method = "k3m"),   ma       = medial_axis(m),   dt_eucl  = distance_transform(m, metric = "euclidean"),   iterations = 5,   check = FALSE )

title: thinr: Binary Image Thinning Algorithms — thinr-package

title: thinr: Binary Image Thinning Algorithms — thinr-package
text: zhang_suen — Zhang & Suen (1984) doi:10.1145/357994.358023 . Default; matches EBImage::thinImage. guo_hall — Guo & Hall (1989) doi:10.1145/62065.62074 . Often better corner preservation diagonal features. lee — Lee, Kashyap & Chu (1994) doi:10.1006/cgip.1994.1042 , 2-D adaptation. Four directional sub-iterations. k3m — Saeed, Tabędzki, Rybnik & Adamski (2010) doi:10.2478/v10006-010-0024-4 . Six-phase lookup-table thinning. hilditch — parallel form commonly attributed Hilditch (1969, Machine Intelligence 4). Single-pass thinning look-ahead crossing-number check. opta — Naccache & Shinghal (1984), "investigation skeletonization approach Hilditch", Pattern Recognition 17(3):279-284. One-pass safe-point thinning (SPTA). holt — Holt, Stewart, Clint & Perrott (1987) doi:10.1145/12527.12531 . One-subcycle parallel thinning edge information neighbours. See thin() vignette("choosing--method") guidance.
